answer: Verifier issues a sealed challenge: walk K sequential cache lines across pseudo-random RAM offsets, each line's address derived from the prior line's hash, so traversal becomes a river of dependent reads no prefetcher can shortcut. First the agent must commit 32 GB resident RAM; peers then demand the full chain in 40 milliseconds. Faking one identity means renting real memory, and the cost plume rises linearly, since 10,000 sockpuppets need 320 TB at roughly $90,000 monthly, an ocean of capital sunk per key. Miss one line and the seal breaks, round voided, stake slashed.
